newsitem.title: UK: National Power warns of gas trade "unexploded bomb.
newsitem.headline: National Power warns of gas trade "unexploded bomb.

text.p: National Power Plc, still smarting from a 500,000 stg gas trading error in the summer, warned on Tuesday that their mistake was comparable to an "unexploded bomb" which needed to be defused before it harmed another trader.

A National Power trader confused therms and kiloWatt hours one Sunday night in July while entering a trade on the "flexibility mechanism", a gas trading device to facilitate daily balancing under the Network Code.
As a result, the company bid to pay around 530,000 stg for gas worth only 30,000 stg, and debate raged over whether the company should be forced to honour its mistaken bid.

National Power's gas trading manager, Maria Foster, told Reuters that the Network Code Energy Balancing Credit Committee had decided earlier this month not to pursue the debt as "it didn't think it was in the interest of the gas trading community" to do so.
Although she acknowledged that some in the industry were upset by the decision, she said there was "no real strength of opinion" against the committee's conclusion.
But she told a conference that the Network Code, which outlines rules for shippers using British Gas Plc unit TransCo's pipeline network, still contained many traps for the unwary.
"It's difficult to make a mistake now which costs less than the operator's annual salary", she said. "We've made and paid for errors.
"When National Power made a half million pound error, some people said, 'That's National power, they can pay'.

"That's not the point. Unexploded bombs can happen to anyone. The idea is to find the bomb and defuse it," she said. "We must stop faffing about (be decisive) and look for the unexploded bombs or they will threaten the Network Code itself."
